To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the `1-regularization error is of order n-1/2 for linear regression and that the `1-penalty is a good oracle for this problem.

(i) the prediction error of `1- regularized linear regression is of order n-1/2 for any number of covari- ables, even if it is substantially larger than n, and (ii) this prediction error is within a logarithmic factor of the error of the best possible estimator.

the `1-regularization method for linear regression is persistent with respect to the sample size n (in the sense that the prediction risk of the regularized estimator is close to that of the oracle, i.e. the best possible linear estimator) with rate O(log n), and that this rate is optimal in the sense that it is the best possible rate of persistence for linear regression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of predicting a real-valued response variable y from a large collection of covariates x.
the following question: how well can one predict the response of an unknown linear function of a large number of variables, given a sample of noisy observations of this linear function?
the following three topics: (1) Persistence of the LASSO. (2) The LASSO and the Dantzig selector. (3) The LASSLASSO, and the Dantizg selector with the L1 norm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the `1-regularization procedure is able to achieve the best possible prediction error, in the sense that it can achieve the error of the best linear predictor, with the same order of magnitude, in the same number of iterations, and without any additional assumptions.
the `1-regularization procedure is very effective, and it performs well for all sample sizes and all numbers of covariates, even in the case where the covariates are not uniformly bounded.

, for any given sample size, the `1-regularization procedure has the ability to select a model with an error close to the best model in the class of all models with a given number of parameters, and this is true even when the number of covariables is much larger than the sample.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the `1-regularization method is a powerful tool for linear regression and it can be used to estimate high-dimensional vectors with a small error.
the `1-penalty is a very good choice for the prediction of linear models.

, in the case of linear regression, the Lasso estimator (which is a special case of `1- regularized linear regression) has a similar performance to that of the best linear estimator in the class of all estimators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a wide variety of settings, a small number of covariations can explain a large proportion of the variability of the outcome variable, even if the true number of covariants is large.
the “oracle inequality” holds for a wide range of regularization parameters.
`1-regularization has a strong tendency to select variables that have large regression coefficients.
